rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A ray passing through a **parallel-sided slab** refracts towards the normal at the first face and away at the second; because the faces are parallel the internal angles match, so the emergent angle equals the incident angle (i = e) and the emergent ray is **parallel** to the incident one.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - x = t sin(i − r)/cos r - i = e (slab); r same at both faces

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Parallel, not coincident:** the emergent ray keeps the incident direction but sits displaced sideways by x.  ·  **i = e for a slab** — the two refractions cancel in angle, not in position.

rows.text: **Short (2m): Why is the lateral shift zero at normal incidence?** — At i = 0 the ray enters without bending (r = 0); the incident and emergent paths are collinear, so sin(i − r) = 0 and x = 0.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Parallel faces cancel the bending but not the displacement** — the essence of slab refraction.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: x = t sin(i − r)/cos r; emergent ray ∥ incident ray.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: At normal incidence (i = 0), sin(i − r) = 0 and the shift vanishes — the ray passes straight through.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Slab That Shifts but Doesn't Bend Light through a thick glass window comes out parallel to where it started — yet shifted sideways. That **lateral shift** explains why a thick slab never quite lines up with itself and why refracted images through panes look slightly displaced.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2024) ### 2.1 Refraction through a parallel-sided slab A ray striking a glass slab of thickness t: 1. Bends **towards the normal** entering glass (air → glass: r < i). 2. Travels inside and meets the second face. 3. Bends **away from the normal** leaving glass (glass → air: e = i).…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 70:** the slab works because Snell's law is reversible — air→glass and glass→air with the same r cancel. - **To Topic 73:** if the internal angle exceeded the critical angle, the second face would totally reflect — the slab becomes a light guide.…
